correctness.rationale: A fixed geometric point has an invariant nonempty support simplex, and conversely its barycenter is fixed. For prime p a nonidentity rotation generates the whole cyclic group and every complete orbit of an edge is a spanning cycle; containing it guarantees connectivity even after any one vertex is removed. For composite n a proper divisor d≥2 gives a nonempty rotation-invariant union of d disconnected step-d components (single edges when n/d=2). Babson et al., Theorem 3.1, gives a wedge of (n−2)! spheres of dimension 2n−5 for exactly this spanning non-2-connected graph complex. For p≥5 it is simply connected; freeness makes the quotient a regular covering with deck group C_p. Writing m=2p−5, the fibration over BC_p has no positive fibre (co)homology below m; differentials with the first possibly nonzero fibre row cannot affect the base row in degrees ≤m−1. The cyclic two-periodic resolution yields the odd integral homology Z/p and vanishing positive even homology there, and the integral polynomial generator of degree two with relation pu=0. Natural pullback yields the claimed products through degree 2p−6 and the unnormalized category bound p−2. No claim is made for p=3 about that range or the universal cover. Independent finite replay `python3 /workspace/review_calculations/small_cases.py graphs` obtains face counts 6,53,785,21399 and Euler characteristics 0,−1,−5,−23, with no fixed nonempty faces at 3,5 and fixed faces at 4,6. It checks boundary cases, not the integral cup products.
